therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Parkinson's disease patients with motor fluctuations (OFF episodes)
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from pre-dose to 90 minutes post-dose in MDS-UPDRS Part III score after 4 weeks of dosing

results.effect_size: Mean difference 0.23 (95% CI: -3.16 to 3.62) on MDS-UPDRS Part III scale (APL-130277 vs subcutaneous apomorphine); APL LS mean change -13.55, SC LS mean change -13.78
results.target_engagement_evidence: Both arms showed clinically meaningful reductions in MDS-UPDRS Part III scores (~13.5–13.8 points), consistent with dopamine receptor engagement
safety_signals: Intestinal ischaemia reported in 1 patient on subcutaneous apomorphine during Part A dose titration
Intestinal obstruction reported in 1 patient on APL-130277 during Part B
Foot fracture reported in 1 patient on subcutaneous apomorphine during Part B

dose_info.dose: Determined in Part A dose titration

context.indication: Motor OFF episodes associated with Parkinson's disease

results_by_chain.endpoint: MDS-UPDRS Part III change from pre-dose to 90 minutes post-dose at Week 4
